minor.issue: Omits reduced internal carotid artery cross-sectional area and the moderating effect on peak pulse pressure, both reported as main results; notes only that head-impact exposure differed in one study without detail (>50 g impacts higher in collar group).

Omits the authors' stated limitations that most studies randomized at team level and that the visible collar meant participants and observers knew allocation; 'low to very low for most outcomes' slightly understates that head-impact and blast exposure were graded moderate.
Inclusion criteria specified observational designs although all 15 included studies were described as RCTs; the record does not flag this inconsistency.
Single sentence of aim only; no study count, populations or results.
No effect values or GRADE certainty ratings (e.g., concussion incidence: 1 study, very low certainty; white matter: low).
Omits named databases, 2000-2024 window, RoB 2 and GRADE appraisal.
Advice about riskier contact behaviour and symptom reporting is reasonable but not drawn from the review.
Should state the review did not evaluate recovery or return to sport rather than issuing device guidance.

note: Both are accurate and appropriately cautious; A is more specific on methods, values and GRADE certainty, while B better captures the team-level randomisation, unblinded visible device and full set of vascular findings, so neither clearly dominates.
